text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.6% today to $132.46, recovering from a four-day slide that had knocked the stock down nearly 3% through Thursday. The bounce came as oil prices spiked—Brent crude jumped 3% to above $90 a barrel after the U.S. struck Iranian targets, the first such military action in weeks. Since ConocoPhillips is a major oil producer, higher crude prices directly improve its earnings prospects and cash flow.

The stock also benefited from a broader tailwind in the energy sector: the White House announced it will meet with U.S. oil refiners to discuss boosting refining capacity, signaling political support for the industry at a time when gas prices are a concern heading into the midterm election. Meanwhile, geopolitical tensions—U.S.-Iran strikes and Russia's threatened strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure—are creating uncertainty around global oil supply, which typically pushes prices higher and favors producers.
